sentences.text: Arrival regulation begins when the Demand Prediction Service shows that inbound demand will exceed the Airport Acceptance Rate within the planning horizon.
The Regional Flow Manager evaluates regulation options in the Arrival Regulation Console using runway availability, sector load, stand readiness, and forecast weather as the controlling inputs.
The preferred option in Normal Operations is a minor time-based sequence adjustment that moves delay to upstream departure points rather than to airborne holding near Meridian.
When the imbalance is larger, the Slot Allocation Engine can support a Ground Delay Program that meters selected arrivals before they depart for the region.
The Regional Flow Manager uses the restriction notice to bound the arrival regulation timeline before committing new landing-rate values in the Arrival Regulation Console.
The Capacity Assessment Module calculates candidate Airport Acceptance Rate values for each runway configuration and exposes the operational basis for each value on the Common Situation Display.
The Tower Supervisor confirms whether the proposed landing rate is compatible with runway occupancy, missed approach protection, and local spacing constraints.
The Airspace Sector Planner confirms whether terminal and en-route sector loads can absorb the regulated stream without generating unsafe compression.

The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the proposed treatment for network impact and identifies flights where upstream delay would create a disproportionate connection or aircraft rotation penalty.
The Slot Coordinator then uses the Slot Allocation Engine to distribute arrival times according to the approved business rules and any protected flight criteria in the Business Rules Registry.
The Airport CDM Portal presents the resulting arrival plan to Aircraft Operator Representative users and records acknowledgements in the Collaborative Decision Log.
Airborne holding prevention is the primary design objective because excess holding increases fuel burn, controller workload, and the likelihood of unplanned diversion.
The Arrival Regulation Console therefore issues alerts before predicted holding stacks form, not after airborne delay has already accumulated.
The Sector Load Monitor contributes early warnings when converging arrival flows are projected to exceed terminal sector capacity under the current metering plan.
The Weather Ingest Gateway updates the arrival model when wind shifts, visibility reductions, or convective activity change achievable runway throughput.
If weather or runway conditions degrade faster than the model forecast, the Regional Flow Manager may apply a tactical landing-rate reduction for a defined review interval.

If conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager may approve a staged landing-rate increase, but the increase is limited until the Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing and runway occupancy performance.

Diversion triggers are monitored continuously and include predicted holding beyond operator fuel thresholds, loss of required approach capability, sustained sector saturation, and runway availability below the minimum safe acceptance rate.

The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with affected airline control centers when diversion risk becomes material so that alternate airport decisions can be made before fuel margins become critical.

The Emergency Response Coordinator is informed when a diversion trigger is associated with an aircraft condition that could affect rescue and firefighting readiness at Meridian or at an alternate airport.
During Adverse Weather Mode, tactical adjustments are reviewed more frequently because landing-rate stability may depend on short-lived runway configuration and approach spacing opportunities.

During Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Manager may combine arrival regulation with departure metering to protect surface balance and prevent inbound aircraft from occupying gates needed for recovery flights.
All rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, and effective times are written to the Audit Event Ledger for later review.

The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded regulation history to compare predicted holding, actual airborne delay, diversion outcomes, and achieved landing rates for continuous improvement of Meridian arrival management.
